title: Possessing the living
summary: How a demon can take a host who has not died.

claims.text: Most fallen enter the newly dead, whose souls are pushed out leaving only scraps of memory. Sometimes a demon instead takes a person who is still alive, and that fuller human soul may push back harder against the demon within.
Some fallen call such open mortals fontanelles, after their weak membranes: something has worn the spirit thin enough for an escaping demon to find the body and slip in.
A person who cries out in true desperation for something vital, such as revenge, love or death, may draw a fleeing demon that offers a bargain; the price is nearly always possession.
Dabbling occultists who stumble on real rites, or on a book a demon planted, can call a demon to themselves, and some beg for one to come.

Many small cults hide sinister aims behind harmless fronts such as self-help groups, and members led step by step into worshipping strange angels may end by inviting a demon in. Many demons have founded such cults for this purpose.
When a demon takes a living host, the human soul is not driven out but crushed down and trapped inside.
